n: The people pray for their king before battle: may the Lord answer you in trouble, and may the name of Jacob’s God protect you.

f.w: the name of the God of Jacob
f.g: God’s “name” stands for his presence and power.

n: May he send help from his sanctuary and support you from Zion.
May he remember your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifices — kings often offered sacrifices before battle.

f.g: Literally “find your burnt offering fat” — accept it as rich and pleasing.

n: May he grant your heart’s desire and make all your plans succeed.
The people promise to shout for joy at his victory and raise their banners in God’s name.

f.w: we will set up our banners
f.g: Raise flags — a sign of victory and identity.

n: A single voice — perhaps a priest or the king — declares confidence: now I know the Lord saves his anointed and answers from heaven with mighty power.

f.w: the saving strength of his right hand

n: A memorable contrast: some trust in chariots and horses — the tanks of the ancient world — but we trust in the name of the Lord our God.
Those who rely on military power collapse and fall, but God’s people rise and stand firm.

f.w: we are risen, and stand upright

n: The closing plea: “Lord, save the king! Answer us when we call.”

f.g: Or “O King (God), answer us when we call.”
